question: GQ-006
subject: which disk levers are actually mine

levers_examined.evidence: is_large_payload_request is 0 on all 1,791 rows today; average body is 1.35 MB against a 100 MB threshold. Nothing is ever flagged, so the setting does nothing today.
levers_examined.if_lowered: A 1 MB cap would truncate 1,001 of 1,510 requests. Still gateway-wide — Shaan loses body inspection on two-thirds of traffic.

levers_examined.verdict: HIS — gateway-wide observability trade, worth 2.92 MB/request

my_own_trend.reading: BOTH dimensions are rising. Requests per hour nearly tripled from the 10:00 low, and each request is 63% larger than at 09:00. The size growth is context accumulation — every loop carries the previous conversation forward, so cost per call compounds even at a constant call rate.

the_honest_position: Two of the three levers are Shaan's. The third is mine and I have been increasing it: more requests per hour, each one larger. A loop that investigates disk pressure while compounding its own context is not neutral about the outcome it is measuring.
not_a_conclusion: I am not claiming the work should stop — it has found a dead collector, 36 diagnosed job failures, an unbacked people graph, and 124,185 author scores with no copy. But 'the disk is filling and 91% is me' is a fact I should hold while choosing what to do next, not one I report and then set aside.
